title: Capacity Sculpting & Pricing Experiment for Dedicated GPU Bands
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Context: Enterprise customers are asking for predictable cost + burstability for Dedicated GPU reservations while avoiding overcommit and complex contract terms. Current offerings (fixed-reserved bands + ad-hoc burst) create negotiation friction and unclear unit economics for both sales and infra.

Objective: Run a pricing & packaging experiment that tests a 'Capacity Sculpting' product: multi-node reserved bands with configurable burst envelopes, graded SLA tiers, and an autoscale grace policy. Goal is to measure conversion uplift for multi-quarter contracts and reduce custom contract negotiation time by 30% for large deals.

Hypothesis: Customers who can commit to a baseline reserved band plus a transparent burst envelope (prepriced credits + defined autoscale safety) will be more likely to sign 12+ month contracts and accept slightly higher baseline unit price in exchange for predictable burstability and SLAs.

Experiment design:
- Offer 3 SKU permutations (Sculpt-Base, Sculpt-Plus, Sculpt-Peak) differentiated by baseline throughput band (expressed in GPU-hours/day), burst envelope size (30% / 60% / 120% of baseline), and SLA latency/throughput guarantees.
- Price model: baseline monthly reservation fee + pre-bundled burst credits + overage rate. Include a rebate curve for sustained baseline utilization >85%.
- Autoscale policy: soft-autoscale (grace window 90s, bounded to burst envelope) for P0/P1 customers; hard cap with failover to hosted model for P2.
- Contract template changes: include explicit burst-credit accounting, preemption and fallback policies, support response SLAs per tier, and a short appendix about audit/KMS requirements.
- Security/Contract QA: prepare answers to top 20 security questionnaire items impacted by private deployments, including KMS integration, tenant isolation, network egress controls, and retained logs retention.

Success metrics:
- Primary: 15% increase in conversion to 12+ month reserved commitments among pilot cohort within 60 days.
- Secondary: 30% reduction in custom clause asks for burst handling in RFCs; <5% incidents caused by autoscale misconfiguration during pilot; negative revenue impact due to bursting < 4% of baseline revenue.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: internal review of pricing matrix and contract appendix (legal + security).
- Week 2: sales pilot with 5 prospects (AMs assigned).
- Week 4: telemetry instrumentation (tokens/GPU-hours per tenant, autoscale events, failed fallbacks), dashboard in Console to track cohort.
- Week 8: analyze results, propose permanent SKU adjustments or discontinue.

Key trade-offs and open questions:
- Pricing sensitivity: do we want aggressive burst discounts to drive adoption or conservative pricing to protect infra spend?
- SLA surface: offering low-latency SLAs across burst envelopes increases operational risk; require clearer failure-mode docs.
- Billing complexity: bundling burst credits adds billing engine work (proration, rollover rules). Need engineering estimate.

Stakeholders: Lukas Romero (PM lead, assignee), Priya Nair (creator, GTM lead), Maya Chen (Sales ENG lead), Ethan Park (Infra lead), Anya Kovalev (Legal), Samir Patel (Security).

Deliverables:
- Pricing matrix CSV + unit economics model (link in attachments).
- Contract appendix draft for legal/security review.
- Pilot customer list and AM playbook.
- Console telemetry dashboard prototype (route: dedicated-sculpting).
